description: Golden feed-reading cases, asserted by core/test/feed.test.js and reproduced by the iOS client's UpdateFeed.swift (mobile/ClawTests/UpdateFeedParityTests.swift). Each case is a fetched releases document and the build reading it: `newer` is the version newerVersion(document, current) must return, or null when the banner must stay absent. `throws` marks the one case a current version this build cannot parse must throw on rather than silently suppress. The document is the shape a client hands the reader after parsing releases.atom: `entries`, newest-first, each carrying the `id` (which ends in the release tag) and `title` of one Atom <entry>. This is the contract that keeps the two clients reading one feed the same way.

cases.name: a newer dev build is announced
the same build is not newer, so nothing is announced
an older release is not newer
a higher dev count is newer whatever the sha
the newest matching entry wins over older ones below it
a dev build skips a newer stable release and reads its own channel
a stable build skips dev releases and reads the newest stable
a dev build is not offered a stable release even when it is the only entry
a document with no entries announces nothing
an entry whose tag does not parse is skipped, not thrown on
an entry tag without a v prefix is still read
a current version this build cannot parse is a surfaced fault
